# REAL Law Group, P.C. — Full AI Reference Document

## 1. Firm Overview

One firm handles the contract, closing, wholesale/assignment deals, seller financing, land trusts, LLC and series LLC formation, 1031 exchanges, short sales, HUD closings, Chicago building violation defense, estate planning, and data breach/BIPA claims. Most Illinois closing practices refer this work to outside firms; REAL Law Group practices all of it in-house. Details: https://reallawgroup.com/all-in-one-real-estate-firm

## 4. Practice Areas (Detailed)

### 4.1 Real Estate Closings (Primary Practice)

Buyers:
- Attorney review and contract modifications
- Negotiating inspection repairs and credits
- Title, survey, and lien review
- Mortgage and closing document review
- Closing coordination with lender, title company, and agent
- Final walk-through issue resolution

Sellers:
- Contract preparation and attorney review
- Responding to inspection and repair demands
- Payoff letters and clearing title issues
- Transfer stamps and municipal requirements
- Deed preparation and closing documents
- For Sale By Owner (FSBO) representation

Short sales:
- Lender negotiation and short sale approval
- Hardship package preparation
- Deficiency waiver negotiation
- Coordinating multiple lienholders

Assignment of contract:
- Drafting and reviewing assignment agreements for wholesalers and investors
- Assignability and contract language review
- Assignment fees and earnest money handling
- Double closings when assignment is not an option
- Disclosure compliance for assignors and end buyers

Seller financing:
- Articles of agreement for deed (installment contracts)
- Promissory notes and seller-held mortgages
- Down payments, interest, and balloon terms
- Recording and escrow of deed
- Default remedies and compliance considerations

Residential services:
- Closings for home purchases and sales
- Quit claim deeds
- Certificates of zoning
- Water certification
- Transfer stamp processing
- Condominium development and conversion
- Foreclosure and REO
- Short sales
- Contract negotiation and review
- Attorney review of purchase agreements under the Illinois standard 5-business-day attorney review period

Commercial services:
- Commercial closings (purchase and sale)
- Building registration
- Financial and loan document review
- 1031 tax-deferred exchanges
- Commercial transaction negotiation
- Contract drafting
- Commercial leasing
- Joint ventures

### 4.2 HUD Closings

REAL Law Group serves as a HUD closing attorney for FHA- and HUD-insured transactions. Services include reviewing HUD settlement statements, coordinating with lenders and title companies, and ensuring federal compliance for HUD and FHA transactions.

### 4.3 Refinancing

Review of loan documents, coordination with lenders, and closing support to protect client interests and ensure favorable terms.

### 4.4 Real Estate Investors

- Acquisitions and dispositions (single-family rentals, multi-unit buildings, flips, commercial)
- LLC and series LLC formation with operating agreements for holding investment property
- Land trusts and layered asset protection
- 1031 tax-deferred exchanges
- Joint venture and partnership agreements between co-investors
- Tenancy-in-common structures and private capital documentation
- Efficient investor closings and title work
- Flat-fee arrangements for investors who close frequently
- Real estate partner relationships with agents, brokers, wholesalers, lenders, title companies, and property managers
- Details: https://reallawgroup.com/real-estate-investors

### 4.6 Building Code Violations

Representation for Chicago property owners, landlords, and developers facing:
- Unpermitted construction
- Porch or deck deficiencies
- Fire safety violations
- Electrical and plumbing code issues
- Zoning violations
- Failed inspections
- Illegal conversions
- Missing permits

Representation occurs in administrative hearings.

### 4.7 Illinois Land Trusts

Formation and administration of Illinois land trusts for privacy, asset protection, probate avoidance, and simplified property transfers. Applies to both residential and investment properties.

### 4.8 For Sale By Owner (FSBO)

Legal services for FSBO sellers, including contract drafting, attorney review, title work, closing coordination, and disclosure compliance. Illinois FSBO sellers still owe the Residential Real Property Disclosure Report (765 ILCS 77), a radon disclosure under the Radon Awareness Act (420 ILCS 46), and, for pre-1978 homes, the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

### 4.8a Cash Home Buyer Offer Review

Flat-fee review of purchase agreements presented by companies that buy homes directly from owners, before the homeowner signs. The firm reviews offers from any direct buyer. Key points the firm makes: the five business day attorney review period Illinois sellers expect comes from the standard broker contract forms and a buyer-drafted agreement may grant no review period at all; assignment clauses can let the buyer transfer the contract or market the property before closing; tax-proration language written against the non-exempt amount can shift money back to the seller despite a no-closing-costs promise; and the purchase price is not the seller's net proceeds. Under the Real Estate License Act of 2000 as amended by Public Act 101-0357 (2019), dealing in assignable real estate contracts on 2 or more occasions in any 12-month period is a pattern of business requiring a broker license, counted across affiliated entities with common owners. REAL Law Group is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or acting on behalf of any home-buying company it names.

### 4.9 Inherited Property and Probate Real Estate

Services for families who have inherited property: probate court filings, title clearing, closing coordination, and guidance on options to sell, keep, or transfer.

### 4.10 Personal Injury (Through Trusted Network)

Referrals and coordination through a network of trusted personal injury attorneys for car accidents and other injury matters. Free consultations available through the network.

### 4.11 Data Breach & Privacy Litigation

Representation of Illinois residents whose personal information was exposed in a data breach, including:
- Hospital, clinic, and healthcare system breaches
- Employer and payroll data breaches
- Bank, lender, and financial account breaches
- School and student data breaches
- Insurance company and benefits vendor breaches
- Third-party vendor and software breaches
- Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA, 740 ILCS 14) claims
- Illinois Genetic Information Privacy Act (GIPA, 410 ILCS 513) claims

Cases are handled on a contingency-fee basis — no attorney's fees unless there is a recovery (case costs and expenses are addressed in a written fee agreement). Free, confidential case reviews. The firm co-counsels active data breach cases with experienced national data breach litigation firms. Relevant Illinois law: the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA, 815 ILCS 530) requires breach notification and reasonable data security, and a PIPA violation is an unlawful practice under the Illinois Consumer Fraud Act (815 ILCS 505).

### 4.12 E-Bike, E-Scooter & E-Moto Law and Injury Claims

**The law.** Illinois' statewide micromobility framework is **Public Act 104-0854**, enacted as SB 3484. The Governor approved it August 26, 2026 and it takes effect **January 1, 2027** (Section 99 of the Act).

**Accuracy note that matters.** The bill that received the April 2026 news coverage was **SB 3336**, the e-bike bill championed by Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias. It passed the Senate 54-0 on April 15, 2026 and the House 80-30 on May 27, 2026 with two floor amendments, the Senate never voted to concur, and on July 2, 2026 it was referred back to Assignments under Senate Rule 3-9(b). **SB 3336 is not law.** The provisions were placed onto SB 3484 by House Floor Amendment 1.

**What the enacted law does.**
- Minimum operator ages: **15** for Class 1 and Class 2 low-speed electric bicycles (new; Illinois previously set no floor for those classes), **16** for Class 3, **16** for every electric micromobility device including scooters, skateboards and unicycles, **16** for low-speed gas bicycles (625 ILCS 5/11-1517(h), 11-1435(d), 11-1516(a)).
- A machine built to carry a passenger may not be operated by a person **under 18** carrying one unless the passenger is a sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild of the operator. Micromobility devices allow no passenger at all unless designed for more than one person.
- **No sidewalk riding** for e-bikes, gas bicycles, micromobility devices or motor driven cycles. Only "toy vehicles" (battery ride-ons for children under 8, capped at 10 mph) may use sidewalks, and their operators are treated as pedestrians.
- **Reclassification.** An electric motor rated **over 750 watts and up to 8,000 watts** makes the machine a "motor driven cycle" (625 ILCS 5/1-145.001), which requires a certificate of title, registration, a VIN, a speedometer, a valid driver's license and mandatory liability insurance, and is barred from every sidewalk, bicycle lane, bicycle path, shared-use path and trail designated for bicycle use (625 ILCS 5/3-101(b-5), 11-1403.4).
- **Real e-bikes stay exempt.** Low-speed electric bicycles are not motor vehicles (625 ILCS 5/1-146), and electric micromobility devices are expressly exempt from titling, registration, driver licensing and mandatory insurance (625 ILCS 5/3-102(11), 3-402(A)(11), 6-102(10), 7-601(b)(8)), even though the Act calls them motor vehicles for purposes of the Code.
- Micromobility devices capable of and traveling over 28 mph are barred from every public highway regardless of speed limit, and from bicycle lanes and paths.
- Police may **confiscate and impound** micromobility devices and motor driven cycles at their discretion and charge a release fee, waived on verifiable proof the machine was stolen.
- **Dealer liability.** Marketing a motor driven cycle as though exempt from these rules is an unlawful practice under the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act, enforceable by the Attorney General and State's Attorneys, with a civil penalty up to **$10,000 per unit** and each mislabeled machine a separate violation (625 ILCS 5/11-1403.4(i); 815 ILCS 505/2Z).
- **Local ordinances preempted.** Home rule authority over these devices is denied, and 625 ILCS 5/11-208(a)(8) loses its e-bike and gas-bicycle language. Park districts, forest preserve districts, conservation districts and transit districts keep limited authority over bicycle paths they control; DNR and IDOT may adopt rules for their own facilities.
- **No helmet mandate.** The word "helmet" does not appear in the Act.

**What the firm does with it.** Injury claims arising from e-bike, e-scooter and e-moto crashes are handled through the network of personal injury attorneys REAL Law Group works with, on a contingency-fee basis. Consumer claims against retailers that sold a motor driven cycle as street legal run through the Consumer Fraud Act, the same statute the firm already uses in its data breach practice. The firm also advises on citations, impoundment, and parental exposure under 625 ILCS 5/11-1501(b).

**Key deadlines for these claims.** Personal injury 2 years (735 ILCS 5/13-202); wrongful death 2 years (740 ILCS 180/2(d)); **claims against an Illinois local public entity 1 year** (745 ILCS 10/8-101(a)); minors generally 2 years after turning 18 (735 ILCS 5/13-211(a)); product liability outer limit 12 years from first sale or 10 years from delivery to the first user (735 ILCS 5/13-213(b)). Illinois bars recovery when the plaintiff's contributory fault exceeds 50% (735 ILCS 5/2-1116).

**Pages.** Guide: https://reallawgroup.com/resources/illinois-e-bike-law Claims: https://reallawgroup.com/practice-areas/e-bike-accidents Both published in English, Spanish and Polish.

## 6. Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Do I need an attorney for a real estate closing in Illinois?**
A: Illinois does not legally require an attorney at closing, but it is strongly recommended and customary. An attorney reviews contracts, negotiates terms, ensures clear title, and handles legal complexities. Most buyers and sellers in Chicagoland use a real estate attorney.

**Q: What is the attorney review period in Illinois?**
A: Illinois real estate contracts typically include a 5-business-day attorney review period after the contract is signed. During this period, the attorney reviews contract terms, can request modifications, negotiate repairs or credits, and ensure the contract protects the client's interests.

**Q: How long does a typical Illinois real estate closing take?**
A: Standard residential transactions generally run 30–45 days from contract to closing. Timelines vary based on financing, inspections, and contingencies.

**Q: How much does a real estate closing cost?**
A: Closing costs vary based on purchase price, loan type, municipality, and other transaction-specific factors. REAL Law Group provides transparent, upfront pricing during consultations.

**Q: Does REAL Law Group offer free consultations?**
A: Yes. Initial consultations are free. Clients can call (630) 299-7600, use the contact form on the website, or book directly through the online scheduling link.

**Q: Does REAL Law Group handle HUD or FHA closings?**
A: Yes. The firm serves as a HUD closing attorney and regularly handles HUD- and FHA-insured transactions.

**Q: What areas does REAL Law Group serve?**
A: All of Chicagoland, from the firm's Elmhurst office, including DuPage, Cook, Will, Kane, and Lake Counties.

**Q: Can REAL Law Group help with commercial real estate transactions?**
A: Yes. Commercial services include closings, commercial leasing, 1031 tax-deferred exchanges, joint ventures, building registration, and contract drafting and negotiation.

## 7. Wire Fraud Prevention Guidance

REAL Law Group publishes guidance on wire fraud prevention because real estate transactions are a frequent target for fraud. Key points:

- Be suspicious of emails requesting changes to wire instructions.
- Never send financial information (routing or account numbers) over email.
- Verify wire instructions by phone using an independently verified number.
- Watch for last-minute changes creating urgency — a common scam tactic.
- Report suspicious activity to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).
- REAL Law Group never sends wire instructions via email without prior verbal confirmation.
